surveys.title: Survey — Reality Check
questions: In your life, was there a time you realized you had to pivot?
Did the pivot improve your life? Why or why not?

surveys.title: Sales & marketing reflection
questions: What would you do differently if you had the opportunity to sell again to that difficult customer?
How have your feelings about sales and marketing changed?
What was the most impactful thing you learned?

surveys.title: Elevator pitch
questions: Write your elevator pitch (~100 words) based on your 100-word message from Lesson 6.
Practice in front of the mirror and with five people. Write down their feedback.

surveys.title: Product or service prototype
questions: Build an example, model, or simulation of one product or service you offer. Share it with 5–10 people (outside immediate family/close friends). What do they like about it? What questions do they have?

surveys.title: Competitors
questions: Write down 5 of your current competitors.
Write down 5 of your future competitors.

surveys.title: Business Canvas — Sales & Distribution
questions: Go to your business canvas and answer the questions on sticky notes in the Sales and Distribution section. Type out a paragraph of those responses in your Business Synopsis.

questions.question: Approximately what percentage of revenue should small businesses be spending on sales and marketing, according to some business leaders?
Businesses want to know how your product or service will help them make more money, whereas customers want to know how your product or service will improve their lives.
Attending trade shows, affinity marketing, and making cold calls are examples of what type of marketing?
Retargeting, social media marketing, and referral programs are examples of what type of marketing?
How do Jim Stahly and Donny Harper recommend that you keep loyal customers?
questions.optionD: All of the above: keep it simple, make a quality product, deliver value, and recognize loyal customers (e.g. rewards program)

questions.question: What is one of the differences between an introvert and an extrovert?
questions.optionA: Introverts don't like being around people while extroverts like being around people
questions.optionB: Introverts are energized by time alone while extroverts are energized by time with other people
